akhfash:11-11.t:
And He said ﴿لاَغِيَةً﴾, that is: you will not hear a word of idle talk (لغو), and He made it ﴿لاَغِيَةً﴾. The proof for this is that you say "فارِس" for the owner of a horse (فَرَس), "دارِع" for the owner of a coat of mail (دِرْع), and "شاعر" for the possessor of poetry (شِعْر). And the poet said [in the majzūʾ al-kāmil metre; this is the two hundred and seventy-eighth verse cited as evidence]:
* أَغررتَنِي وَزَعَمْتَ أَنَّكَ لابِنٌ بِالصَّيْفِ تامِرْ *
(Did you deceive me, claiming that in summer you are a man of milk and a man of dates?)
That is: an owner of milk and an owner of dates. «[Translator's note: the source gives this verse the same number as the verse cited at 81:4.]»

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿هَلْ﴾: indeed ﴿أَتَاكَ حَدِيثُ الْغَاشِيَةِ﴾: the Resurrection, because it overwhelms creation with its terrors.

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾ — by them the persons themselves are meant in both places — ﴿خَاشِعَةٌ﴾: abased,

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿عَامِلَةٌ نَاصِبَةٌ﴾: in toil and weariness with the chains and the fetters.

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿تُصْلَى﴾ — with ḍamma on the tāʾ, and with fatḥa on it [تَصْلَى] — ﴿نَارًا حَامِيَةً﴾

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿لَيْسَ لَهُمْ طَعَامٌ إِلَّا مِنْ ضَرِيعٍ﴾: it is a kind of thorn-plant that no animal grazes on because of its foulness,

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿لَا يُسْمِنُ وَلَا يُغْنِي مِنْ جُوعٍ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ نَاعِمَةٌ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿لِسَعْيِهَا﴾ in the world through obedience ﴿رَاضِيَةٌ﴾ in the Hereafter, when it has seen its reward,

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿فِي جَنَّةٍ عَالِيَةٍ﴾ physically and in rank.

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿لَا يُسْمَعُ﴾ — with yāʾ and with tāʾ [تَسْمَعُ] — ﴿فِيهَا لَاغِيَةٌ﴾, that is, a soul given to laghw, that is, idle talk [لَاغِيَةً].

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿فِيهَا عَيْنٌ جَارِيَةٌ﴾ with water, in the sense of springs.

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿فِيهَا سُرُرٌ مَرْفُوعَةٌ﴾ in themselves, in worth and in place,

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿وَأَكْوَابٌ﴾: cups without handles ﴿مَوْضُوعَةٌ﴾ at the edges of the springs, made ready for their drinking,

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿وَنَمَارِقُ﴾: cushions ﴿مَصْفُوفَةٌ﴾: one beside another, to be leaned on,

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿وَزَرَابِيُّ﴾: carpets, rugs with pile, ﴿مَبْثُوثَةٌ﴾: spread out.

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿أَفَلَا يَنْظُرُونَ﴾, that is, the disbelievers of Mecca, with a look of reflection ﴿إِلَى الْإِبِلِ كَيْفَ خُلِقَتْ﴾

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿وَإِلَى السَّمَاءِ كَيْفَ رُفِعَتْ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿وَإِلَى الْجِبَالِ كَيْفَ نُصِبَتْ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿وَإِلَى الْأَرْضِ كَيْفَ سُطِحَتْ﴾, that is, spread out, so that they may take them as evidence of the power of Allah the Exalted and His oneness. It begins with the camels because they are more closely involved with them than with anything else. His words «سطحت» are apparent in [indicating] that the earth is flat (saṭḥ) — and this is the position of the scholars of the Sharia — not a sphere, as the astronomers (ahl al-hayʾa) say, even though [the latter view] does not overturn any of the pillars of the Sharia.

celaleyn:21-21.t: ﴿فَذَكِّرْ﴾ them of Allah's blessings and the proofs of His oneness; ﴿إِنَّمَا أَنْتَ مُذَكِّرٌ﴾

celaleyn:22-22.t: ﴿لَسْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ بِمُسَيْطِرٍ﴾ — in one reading [بِمُصَيْطِرٍ], with ṣād instead of sīn — that is, given authority over them. This was before the command to wage jihad.

celaleyn:23-23.t: ﴿إِلَّا﴾: but ﴿مَنْ تَوَلَّى﴾: turned away from faith ﴿وَكَفَرَ﴾ in the Qur'an,

celaleyn:24-24.t: ﴿فَيُعَذِّبُهُ اللَّهُ الْعَذَابَ الْأَكْبَرَ﴾: the punishment of the Hereafter; the lesser is the punishment of this world by killing and captivity.

celaleyn:25-25.t: ﴿إِنَّ إِلَيْنَا إِيَابَهُمْ﴾: their return after death,

celaleyn:26-26.t: ﴿ثُمَّ إِنَّ عَلَيْنَا حِسَابَهُمْ﴾: their recompense; We will never leave it.

daas-irab:1-1.t: ﴿هَلْ﴾: an interrogative particle; ﴿أَتاكَ﴾: a past verb and its object; ﴿حَدِيثُ الْغاشِيَةِ﴾: postponed fāʿil (agent), muḍāf to الغاشية; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿وُجُوهٌ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾: an adverb of time annexed to one like it; ﴿خاشِعَةٌ﴾: the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; the clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿عامِلَةٌ ناصِبَةٌ﴾: two further predicates (khabar) of وجوه.

daas-irab:4-4.t: ﴿تَصْلى﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿ناراً﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿حامِيَةً﴾: naʿt (adjective); the clause is a further khabar (predicate) of وجوه.

daas-irab:5-5.t: ﴿تُسْقى﴾: a passive imperfect verb, its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) being latent (mustatir); ﴿مِنْ عَيْنٍ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿آنِيَةٍ﴾: naʿt (adjective); the clause is a second adjective of نار.

daas-irab:6-6.t: ﴿لَيْسَ﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb; ﴿لَهُمْ﴾: the fronted khabar (predicate) of laysa; ﴿طَعامٌ﴾: its postponed noun; ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); ﴿مِنْ ضَرِيعٍ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of طعام; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿لا﴾: negative; ﴿يُسْمِنُ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of ضريع; ﴿وَلا يُغْنِي﴾: conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿مِنْ جُوعٍ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb.

daas-irab:8-8.t: The i'rab of one like it has already been given.

daas-irab:9-9.t: ﴿لِسَعْيِها﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) what follows them; ﴿راضِيَةٌ﴾: a second khabar (predicate) of وجوه.

daas-irab:10-10.t: ﴿فِي جَنَّةٍ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted further khabar (predicate) of وجوه; ﴿عالِيَةٍ﴾: naʿt (adjective) of جنة.

daas-irab:11-11.t: ﴿لا﴾: negative; ﴿تَسْمَعُ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿فِيها﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿لاغِيَةً﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of جنة.

daas-irab:12-12.t: ﴿فِيها﴾: fronted khabar (predicate); ﴿عَيْنٌ﴾: postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿جارِيَةٌ﴾: naʿt (adjective) of عين; the clause is a third adjective of جنة.

daas-irab:13-13.t: Its i'rab is like the preceding one.

daas-irab:14-14.t: ﴿وَأَكْوابٌ﴾: conjoined to سرر; ﴿مَوْضُوعَةٌ﴾: naʿt (adjective) of أكواب.

daas-irab:16-16.t: Also conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:17-17.t: ﴿أَفَلا﴾: the hamza is for interrogation, the fāʾ is a conjunction and لا is negative; ﴿يَنْظُرُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ) by the presence of the nūn, the wāw being its fāʿil (agent); the clause is conjoined to an omitted clause; ﴿إِلَى الْإِبِلِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿كَيْفَ﴾: an interrogative noun in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿خُلِقَتْ﴾: a passive past verb, its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) being latent (mustatir); the clause is a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl, a substitute) for الإبل.

daas-irab:21-22.t:
﴿فَذَكِّرْ﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ indicating an implied condition), and an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the apodosis of an implied condition and has no grammatical position. ﴿إِنَّما﴾: the restraining particle (kāffa) and the restrained one (makfūfa); ﴿أَنْتَ مُذَكِّرٌ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the clause gives the reason (taʿlīl).
﴿لَسْتَ﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb and its noun; ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) what follows them; ﴿بِمُصَيْطِرٍ﴾: the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and ﴿مصيطر﴾ is genitive in form, accusative in position, the khabar of laysa; the clause gives the reason.

daas-irab:23-23.t: ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of exception; ﴿مَنْ﴾: a relative noun, the excepted; ﴿تَوَلَّى﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of من; ﴿وَكَفَرَ﴾: conjoined to تولى.

daas-irab:24-24.t: ﴿فَيُعَذِّبُهُ﴾: the fāʾ occurs in the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) because of the conditional sense in the relative noun, and an imperfect verb and its object; ﴿اللَّهُ﴾: the Name of Majesty, its fāʿil (agent); ﴿الْعَذابَ﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); ﴿الْأَكْبَرَ﴾: naʿt (adjective); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject).

daas-irab:25-25.t: ﴿إِنَّ﴾: a particle resembling the verb (one of inna and its sisters); ﴿إِلَيْنا﴾: the fronted khabar (predicate) of inna; ﴿إِيابَهُمْ﴾: its postponed noun; the clause gives the reason (taʿlīl) and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:26-26.t: Conjoined to what precedes it, and the i'rab is clear.

dervis-irab:1-26.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْغاشِيَةِ) The Resurrection, because it overwhelms (taghshā) creatures. In al-Mukhtār: "al-ghishāʾ: the covering; and 'a covering (ghishāwa) was placed over his sight', with ḍamma, fatḥa or kasra on the ghayn." In al-Miṣbāḥ: "It is said that al-ghashy is the suspension of the motive faculties and the sensitive veins through weakness of the heart, because of severe pain, or cold, or excessive hunger. It is said that al-ghashy is fainting (ighmāʾ); and it is said that ighmāʾ is the filling of the ventricles of the brain with cold, thick phlegm; and it is said that ighmāʾ is a lapse that overtakes a person with a slackening of the limbs due to an ailment. And ghashītuhu, aghshāhu (of the pattern taʿiba), means I came to him, and the noun is al-ghishyān, with kasra."
(آنِيَةٍ) It has reached its anā in heat. In the Qāmūs: "anā al-ḥamīm: its heat reached its limit, so it is ān, and 'this reached its anāhu', also with kasra, i.e. its utmost limit."
(ضَرِيعٍ) In the Qāmūs: "al-ḍarīʿ, like amīr, is the shibraq or its dried form; or a plant whose fresh form is called shibraq and whose dry form is ḍarīʿ, which no beast approaches because of its foulness; and al-sullāʾ and the fresh ʿawsaj; or a plant in stagnant water that has roots which do not reach the earth; or something of Hell more bitter than aloes, fouler than carrion and hotter than fire; and a stinking plant the sea casts up; and the dried form of every tree; and wine, or its thin part; and the skin over the bone beneath the flesh." In al-Kashshāf: "al-ḍarīʿ is dried shibraq, a kind of thorn which camels graze as long as it is fresh; when it dries the camels avoid it, and it is a deadly poison. Abū Dhuʾayb said:
رعى الشبرق الريان حتى إذا ذوى ... وعاد ضريعا بان عنه النحائص
(It grazed the lush shibraq, until, when it withered and became ḍarīʿ, the she-camels left it.)
And he said:
وحبسن في هزم الضريع فكلها ... حدباء دامية اليدين حرود)
(They were held back in the hollows of the ḍarīʿ, and each is humped, bloody in the forefeet, and obstinate.)"
(نَمارِقُ) The plural of namruqa, with ḍamma or kasra on the nūn, two dialects, the first being the better known; it is a small cushion. In the Qāmūs: "al-namruqa, with three vowelings, is the small cushion, or the heaped-up one, or the carpet over the saddle."
(زَرابِيُّ) In the Qāmūs: "al-zarābī are cushions and spreads, or everything that is spread and leaned upon; the singular is zirbī, with kasra, or with ḍamma." The ṭanāfis is also the plural of ṭinfisa, with three vowelings on the ṭāʾ and the fāʾ, so it has nine dialect forms; it is what is now called the prayer rug (sajjāda).
(مَبْثُوثَةٌ) Scattered about the gathering-place.
(بِمُصَيْطِرٍ) Set in authority over them. مسيطر is a noun that comes only in diminutive form, with no non-diminutive: like their words ruwaydan, al-thurayyā, kumayt, mubayqir, mubayṭir and muhaymin. In one reading it is بمسيطر with fatḥa on the ṭāʾ, and this reading is unusual; in Tāj al-ʿArūs: sayṭara is on the pattern fayʿala, so he is musayṭir, and its verb is not used in the passive. We stop in the speech of the Arabs where they stopped; further discussion of the diminutive will come in the section of Benefits.

* I'rab:
(هَلْ أَتاكَ حَدِيثُ الْغاشِيَةِ) هل is an interrogative particle, meaning wonder and stirring up eagerness to listen to the account of al-Ghāshiya. Some made it mean قد, and Ibn Khālawayh made that general for every هل أتاك in the Qur'an; he said: "it means قد أتاك." أتاك is a past verb with a direct object, and حديث الغاشية is the agent. (وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ خاشِعَةٌ عامِلَةٌ ناصِبَةٌ تَصْلى ناراً حامِيَةً تُسْقى مِنْ عَيْنٍ آنِيَةٍ) وجوه is a mubtadaʾ (subject); beginning with it is allowed because of the classification and the description, as will come; يومئذ is an adverbial attached to خاشعة, and the tanwīn in إذ is a compensation for a clause, for which nothing preceded as indication except His word الغاشية, so the clause can be inferred from it, i.e. "on the day when al-Ghāshiya overwhelms"; خاشعة is the khabar (predicate); عاملة and ناصبة are two further predicates. It is also said that خاشعة, عاملة and ناصبة are attributes of the mubtadaʾ and the predicate is the clause تصلى; on the first view the clause تصلى is a fourth predicate; both views are sound and good. نارا is a direct object; it was read with ḍamma on the tāʾ (tuṣlā), in which case نارا is a second object and the deputy agent is latent; حامية is an adjective of النار. تسقى is an imperfect passive verb, its deputy agent latent, its implied form being "it", i.e. faces, meaning their owners; من عين are two [a preposition and its genitive noun] attached to تسقى, and آنية is an adjective of عين. (لَيْسَ لَهُمْ طَعامٌ إِلَّا مِنْ ضَرِيعٍ) A resumptive statement, brought in answer to a question that follows from what preceded, as though it were said: "And what is their food after their drink was mentioned?", so it was said: ليس لهم ...; ليس is a defective past verb; لهم is its fronted predicate; طعام is its postponed noun; إلا is a particle of restriction; and من ضريع is an adjective of طعام or a badal (substitute) for it according to the rule, and it may be in the position of accusative as an exception. (لا يُسْمِنُ وَلا يُغْنِي مِنْ جُوعٍ) The two clauses are adjectives of ضريع, not of طعام, because ḍarīʿ is the one affirmed and it has been denied of both fattening and sufficing against hunger. لا is negative; يسمن is an imperfect verb with its agent "it"; ولا يغني is conjoined to لا يسمن; and من جوع are two [a preposition and its genitive noun] attached to يغني. Al-Shihāb in his gloss on al-Bayḍāwī made من redundant (zāʾida), and on that view جوع is in the position of accusative, the object of يغني. (وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ ناعِمَةٌ، لِسَعْيِها راضِيَةٌ) وجوه is a mubtadaʾ, and beginning with an indefinite is allowed for the sake of classification; the secret of its not being joined by a wāw, as the apparent flow of the context would require, will come in the section of Rhetoric; يومئذ is an adverbial annexed to its like, attached to ناعمة; ناعمة is the khabar of وجوه; ولسعيها are two [a preposition and its genitive noun] attached to راضية; and راضية is a second khabar of وجوه. (فِي جَنَّةٍ عالِيَةٍ، لا تَسْمَعُ فِيها لاغِيَةً) في جنة is a second khabar of وجوه; عالية is an adjective of وجوه «[Translator's note: the source says "an adjective of وجوه", but the adjective evidently belongs to جنة.]» and the clause لا تسمع etc. is a second adjective of جنة; لا is negative; تسمع is an imperfect verb, nominative, its agent "you" (it was also read with tāʾ [for the feminine]); وفيها are two [a preposition and its genitive noun] attached to تسمع; and لاغية is a direct object; it is in the sense of relation (nisba), i.e. a word possessing idle talk, or on ascribing idle talk to it figuratively. (فِيها عَيْنٌ جارِيَةٌ) The clause is a third adjective of جنة; وفيها is a fronted predicate; عين is a postponed mubtadaʾ; and جارية is an adjective of عين. (فِيها سُرُرٌ مَرْفُوعَةٌ وَأَكْوابٌ مَوْضُوعَةٌ وَنَمارِقُ مَصْفُوفَةٌ وَزَرابِيُّ مَبْثُوثَةٌ) The clause is a fourth attribute of جنة; وفيها is a fronted predicate; عين is a postponed mubtadaʾ; and جارية is an adjective of عين [Translator's note: the source repeats here the parsing of the previous verse, evidently by oversight; for this verse it should be سرر as the postponed mubtadaʾ, مرفوعة its adjective]; and what follows is conjoined to it. (أَفَلا يَنْظُرُونَ إِلَى الْإِبِلِ كَيْفَ خُلِقَتْ) A resumptive statement brought to confirm what passed of the account of al-Ghāshiya; the hamza is for denunciatory interrogation and the فاء is for conjunction upon an implied clause that the situation calls for, the implied form being: "Do they deny the resurrection, and do they not look?"; لا is negative; ينظرون is an imperfect verb, nominative; وإلى الإبل are two [a preposition and its genitive noun] attached to it; كيف is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); خلقت is a past passive verb, its agent latent, its implied form being "it", and the clause is a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) from الإبل. ينظرون is transitive to الإبل by means of إلى, and transitive to كيف by way of suspension (taʿlīq). A clause containing an interrogative may be substituted for the noun before it even if that has no interrogative in it, with disagreement about this, as in their saying "I knew Zayd, whose father is he?" The Arabs also put إلى before كيف, and say "إلى كيف يصنع". كيف is a question about a state, and the operative on it is خلقت; and when the operative is suspended from the interrogative within it, the interrogative does not remain in its true sense. Al-Zamakhsharī has a fine passage, which we give here: "'Do they not look at the camel' with a look of consideration, 'how it was created', created wondrously, indicating a Determiner who determined, witnessing to a Planner who planned, in that He created it to rise with heavy loads and haul them to distant lands. So He made it kneel so as to be loaded close to the ground and with ease, then rise with what it carries, and subjected it, docile to whoever leads it by its halter-ropes, neither defying the weak nor resisting the young; and He fashioned it long-necked to rise under heavy loads. It is reported of one of the sages that he was told about the camel and the marvel of its creation, he having grown up in a land
with no camels, so he reflected and then said: 'It must be long-necked.' And when He intended them to be the ships of the land, He made them patient in bearing thirst, so that their intervals between drinking extend to ten days and more; and He made them graze on everything that grows in the wilds and the deserts, of what other beasts do not graze." As for الإبل, it is a collective noun (ism jamʿ) having no singular from its own wording; its singulars are baʿīr, nāqa and jamal. The wording of the Qāmūs:
"al-Ibil, with two kasras and a sukūn on the bāʾ, is feminine, a singular that applies to the plural, being neither a plural nor a collective noun; its plural is ābāl and its diminutive ubayla; and it also means the cloud that carries rain-water." On this basis it would be sound for it to mean the clouds, so that the mention would be arranged by its sequence; but this does not agree with the ease of the Qur'an's exposition and composition; it brought it in sequence with the sky, the earth and the mountains only because the Arabs in their deserts and valleys are used to seeing all of them, so the mention was arranged with these things. (وَإِلَى السَّماءِ كَيْفَ رُفِعَتْ وَإِلَى الْجِبالِ كَيْفَ نُصِبَتْ وَإِلَى الْأَرْضِ كَيْفَ سُطِحَتْ) A statement conjoined to what preceded, like it in its parsing. Ibn Khālawayh, quoting al-Zamakhsharī, said: "It is reported of Hārūn al-Rashīd that he read: كيف سطحت with shadda, but the reading is with lightening, because the whole community agreed on it." (فَذَكِّرْ إِنَّما أَنْتَ مُذَكِّرٌ لَسْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ بِمُصَيْطِرٍ) The فاء is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, i.e. "if they do not look at these things with a look of consideration, reflection and contemplation, then remind them." فذكر is an imperative verb, its agent a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you", and its object omitted, i.e. "remind them, and do not press them, since their guidance is not upon you"; إنما: ما is kāffa (restraining) and the particle is restrained; أنت is a mubtadaʾ; مذكر is the khabar; the clause إنما أنت is a justification for the command to remind; لست is ليس with its noun; عليهم are two [a preposition and its genitive noun] attached to مسيطر; the باء is a redundant preposition; and مسيطر is genitive by the باء in wording and accusative in position, because it is the predicate of ليس. (إِلَّا مَنْ تَوَلَّى وَكَفَرَ فَيُعَذِّبُهُ اللَّهُ الْعَذابَ الْأَكْبَرَ) إلا is a particle of exception; من is excepted, as a connected exception, from the object of فذكر or from the هاء in عليهم. It is also said that the exception is disconnected and إلا means لكن, its operation voided, and من is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause فيعذبه; both views are good and possible. The clause تولى is the ṣila of من, and وكفر is conjoined to the ṣila; the clause إلا من تولى وكفر is in the position of accusative as a disconnected exception, and this is a clause that is annexed to the clauses that have a position in i'rab. The فاء is a linker because of the sense of condition in the relative noun; يعذبه is an imperfect verb, nominative; the هاء is a direct object; الله is the agent; and العذاب is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). It is strange that Ibn Khālawayh parsed it as a second direct object; and Ibn Hishām was right when he established that Ibn Khālawayh was one of the weak grammarians. الأكبر is an adjective of العذاب. (إِنَّ إِلَيْنا إِيابَهُمْ ثُمَّ إِنَّ عَلَيْنا حِسابَهُمْ) The clause has no position, because it is a justification of the greatest punishment; إن is a particle resembling the verb; إلينا is the fronted predicate of إن; إيابهم is its postponed noun; ثم is a conjunction of delay, whose secret will come in the section of Rhetoric; and what follows is conjoined to what precedes, like it in its parsing.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying «لا يسمن ولا يغني من جوع» is the art of completion (tatmīm), which has been treated many times. His saying ولا يغني من جوع is a clause that cannot be dropped from the speech, because when He said لا يسمن, someone could imagine that this food, which is not of the kind of human food, is denied the attribute of fattening, but retains the attribute of sufficing; so the clause ولا يغني من جوع came as a completion of the intended meaning, namely that this food is denied the attribute of giving fatness and strength as it is denied the attribute of removing and dispelling hunger. Some made it a case of negating a thing by affirming it, on the model of the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays «على لاحب لا يهتدى بمناره» (upon a clear road not guided by its landmark), i.e. it has no landmark at all, and as you say "so-and-so has no shade except the sun", meaning to negate the shade emphatically. That is not remote, but the first is firmer and further from strain.
2- Omission (ḥadhf): we have spoken much in this book about omission, and here we shall devote a glimpse to the omission of the direct object in particular, to add benefit, on the occasion of His saying «فذكّر إنما أنت مذكّر». We say: the direct object may be omitted for a purpose, either verbal, such as the harmony of the verse-endings, as in His saying «ما ودعك ربك وما قلى», where the original is "وما قلاك", the object being omitted to harmonize with His saying «والضحى والليل إذا سجى», and such as concision, as in His saying «فإن لم تفعلوا ولن تفعلوا», where the original is "فإن لم تفعلوه ولن تفعلوه", i.e. bringing a surah like it; or semantic, such as showing contempt for it, as in «كتب الله لأغلبنّ أنا ورسلي», i.e. "I shall surely overcome the unbelievers", where the object is omitted to add to its degradation and contempt, or to find it distasteful and shameful to state it, as in the saying of ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her: "He did not see from me, nor did I see from him", i.e. the private parts.
3- In His saying «إن إلينا إيابهم ثم إن علينا حسابهم» is the fronting of the preposition and its genitive noun, the secret in which is emphasis of the threat, that their return is only to the Compeller, able to take vengeance, and that their reckoning is only upon Him. In the conjunction with ثم is an indication of delay in rank, not in time, i.e. it may come directly after the return, but the disparity between the two stations is a matter whose terrors cannot be fathomed, whose extent nobody knows, and which the mind cannot conceive at all. It is not hidden that the report came emphasized with إن, so it is of the "requested" type (khabar ṭalabī), as if they, having hesitated, were in need of emphasis of this matter from which they turned away and which they did not ponder.

* Benefits:
1- The diminutive and its purposes: the first to speak of the diminutive was al-Khalīl ibn Aḥmad, may Allah have mercy on him. It is used for belittling, for magnifying, for compassion, for endearment, for reducing number and for nearing time, and one of them gathered them in his saying:
فعظم وحقر وقرب زماني ... ترحم تحبب رزقت الأماني
وأقلل بتصغيرهم يا فتى ... فما زلت في محفل من معاني
(Magnify, belittle, bring time near; show compassion, show endearment, may you be granted your wishes; and lessen by their diminutive, O young man, for you have not ceased to be in a gathering of meanings.)
Ibn Khālawayh said: "The Arabs make a noun diminutive in praise, not intending belittling by it, as in their saying 'so-and-so is my ṣuddayqī (little friend)' when he is among the truest of his friends. Of that is the saying of ʿUmar about Ibn Masʿūd, 'a little pouch (kunayyif) filled with knowledge', praising him thereby; and the Anṣārī said:
«أنا جذيلها المحكّك وعذيقها المرجّب وحجيرها المؤام»
(I am its rubbing-post, rubbed upon, and its propped-up little palm, and its little enclosure of counsel.)
And of that is that a man said: 'I saw the little bald one (al-uṣaylaʿ), ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, kissing the Stone', intending to praise him by that."
There was disagreement about the saying of ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa in his famous poem rhyming in rāʾ:
وغاب قمير كنت أهوى غروبه ... وروّح رعيان ونوّم سمّر
(And the little moon set, whose setting I desired; the herdsmen brought back their flocks and the night-talkers went to sleep.)
Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, when he heard this verse, said: "What is wrong with him, may Allah fight him: he made small what Allah made great! Allah the Exalted said «والقمر قدّرناه منازل»." Ibn Khālawayh said: "It is possible that Ibn Abī Rabīʿa made qamar diminutive in praise, for what I mentioned; moreover Ibn Abī Rabīʿa recited this poem to Ibn ʿAbbās and he objected to nothing in it. Of that is the saying of a man to his son 'O my little son (yā bunayya)', not intending belittling; so know that. And Ibn Abī Rabīʿa has another argument, which is that the Arabs say of the moon at the end of the month and its beginning 'shafā qumayr', making it diminutive."
What we have mentioned of the meanings of the diminutive is rejected by the Basrans; all that we have mentioned goes back, for them, to the meaning of belittling.
Let us give by way of example the verse of Labīd ibn Rabīʿa, which is:
وكل أناس سوف تدخل بينهم ... دويهية تصفرّ منها الأنامل
(Every people, a little calamity (duwayhiya) will enter among them, from which the fingertips turn yellow.)
The Kufans held that the diminutive in his word دويهية is for magnification, the explanation being that the poet meant by it death, and there is no calamity greater than it. That he meant death is indicated by his describing it with «تصفر منها الأنامل»; the anāmil here are the nails, and they turn yellow only with death. Al-Ṭūsī said in his commentary on the Dīwān of Labīd: "When a man dies or is killed, his fingertips turn yellow and his nails turn black." The Basrans rejected that the diminutive comes for magnification, and al-Raḍī the verifier followed their school, saying: "It is said that the coming of the diminutive for magnification is a case of kināya (allusion), alluding by smallness to reaching the utmost limit, because when a thing exceeds its limit it resembles its opposite. This is answered by saying that its being made diminutive is in accord with people's contempt for it and their disregard of it, for what is meant by it is death, i.e. there comes to them what they despise although it is great in itself, from which the fingertips turn yellow." And the Basrans said of the verse of Labīd: "As for his saying duwayhiya, what is meant is that the smallest of things may corrupt great foundations, so the death of souls may be through the matter that is not heeded." The firmness and strength of this statement are not hidden; so attend to this section, which, though somewhat long, is like beauty: it is never tiresome.
2- Imagination: imaginations differ according to causes, customs and general usage, and so differ among nations. Therefore His saying, in guiding them to infer the wise Maker, «أفلا ينظرون إلى الأمم كيف خلقت» etc. [Translator's note: the source prints "الأمم" (nations) here, evidently a slip for «الإبل» (the camels); the verse is أفلا ينظرون إلى الإبل كيف خلقت.] is denied only by one who does not know that the address is to the Arabs, in whose imagination there is nothing but the camel, because the greater part of their benefit, in their food, clothing and trade, is from it; and there is only an earth that the camels graze, a sky that waters them and it, and mountains that are their strongholds when raids are launched. So it is clear that whoever is acquainted with the conditions of the bedouin Arab knows the reason for the pairing of the mentioned images in their minds, and the reason for their occurring in the Great Qur'an in the stated manner; and whoever of the town-dwellers denies it does so out of ignorance of what the situation requires. How well al-Mutanabbī said:
وكم من عائب قولا صحيحا ... وآفته من الفهم السقيم
(How many a one finds fault with a sound saying, whose affliction is from a sick understanding.)

farraa:6-6.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَّيْسَ لَهُمْ طَعَامٌ إِلاَّ مِن ضَرِيعٍ﴾.
It is a plant called الشِّبْرِق; the people of the Ḥijāz call it الضريع when it is dry, and it is poison.

farraa:11-11.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لاَّ يُسْمَعُ فِيهَا لاَغِيَةً﴾: one who swears to a lie. ʿĀṣim, al-Aʿmash and some readers read: "لا تُسْمَعُ" with tāʾ, and some of the people of Medina read: "لا يُسمع فيها لاغيةٌ". And if it were read: "لا تُسمع فيها لاغيةٌ", it would be as though in agreement with the reading [Translator's note: the sentence is so in the source], because most of the verse-endings are in the nominative.

farraa:13-13.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فِيهَا سُرُرٌ مَّرْفُوعَةٌ﴾.
It is said: مرفوعة means raised high: raised for them, elevated. It is also said: stored away, raised [i.e. kept] for them.

farraa:15-15.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَنَمَارِقُ مَصْفُوفَةٌ﴾.
Some beside others. They are the cushions; the singular is نُمْرُقة. He said: I heard one of [the tribe of] Kalb say: نِمْرِقة, with kasra on the nūn and the rāʾ.

farraa:16-16.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَزَرَابِيُّ مَبْثُوثَةٌ﴾.
They are the carpets that have a fine pile. (مَبْثُوثَةٌ): many.

farraa:17-17.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَفَلاَ يَنظُرُونَ إِلَى ٱلإِبْلِ كَيْفَ خُلِقَتْ﴾.
He made them wonder at the camels' carrying: that they bear their load while kneeling and then rise with it; and none of the beasts can do that except the camel.

farraa:22-22.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَّسْتَ عَلَيْهِم بِمُصَيْطِرٍ﴾.
[You are not] one given dominion. The written text has (بمصيطر) and (المصيطرون) with ṣād, while the reading is with sīn; if it were read with ṣād it would be in accordance with the written text, and it would be correct.

farraa:23-23.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِلاَّ مَن تَوَلَّىٰ وَكَفَرَ﴾.
It may be excepted from the speech upon which the reminding falls, even though it is not mentioned, as you say in speech: "Go and admonish and remind, and include everyone except whoever you have no hope for." Or you may make ﴿مَن تَوَلَّىٰ وَكَفَرَ﴾ disconnected (munqaṭiʿ) from what precedes it, as you say in speech: "We sat talking and discussing good things, except that many people have no desire [for it]"; this is the disconnected [exception].
You recognise the disconnected exception by the fact that إنّ sounds good in the excepted [clause]; when the exception is pure and connected, إنّ does not sound good in it. Do you not see that you say: "I have a hundred except a dirham", and you do not insert إنّ here? This suffices instead of mentioning others.
Some readers and scholars say that (إلا) is equivalent to لكن; that is their explanation of the meaning, but as for (إلا) being fit to stand in place of لكن, no. Do you not see that you say: ما قام عبدالله ولكن زيد (ʿAbd Allāh did not stand, but Zayd [did]), with the wāw expressed or dropped, but you do not say: ما قام عبدالله إلا زيد — unless you intend: ما قام إلا زيد (none stood but Zayd), by repeating the beginning of the speech.
Al-Farrāʾ was asked [136/a] about ﴿إِيَابَهُمْ﴾ (25) [Translator's note: i.e. about reading it with a doubled yāʾ, «إيّابهم»], and he said: it is not permissible in any way.

harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: (هل أتاك حديث الغاشية) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya).

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: His saying «وجوه»: mubtadaʾ (subject); beginning with an indefinite noun is permitted because it has been qualified; «يومئذ»: «يوم» is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) «خاشعة», which is a naʿt (adjective) of «وجوه»; «إذٍ»: an adverbial noun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and the tanwīn is a compensation for a clause indicated by the active participle from «الغاشية», its implied form being: "the day when it overwhelms the people".

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: (عاملة ناصبة) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] Two adjectives (ṣifa) of {وُجُوهٌ}.

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: The clause «تصلى» is the khabar (predicate) of {وُجُوهٌ}.

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: The clause «تسقى» is a second khabar (predicate) of {وُجُوهٌ}; «آنية» is a naʿt (adjective) of «عين».

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: (ليس لهم طعام إلا من ضريع) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is a third khabar (predicate) of {وُجُوهٌ}; «إلا» is for restriction (ḥaṣr); the preposition «من ضريع» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «طعام».

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: The clause «لا يُسمن» is a naʿt (adjective) of {ضَرِيعٍ}

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: «وجوه» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the adverb is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «ناعمة», the naʿt (adjective).

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: The preposition «لسعيها» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «راضية»; «راضية» is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) {وُجُوهٌ}.

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: The preposition «في جنة» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted second khabar (predicate) of {وُجُوهٌ}; «عالية»: naʿt (adjective) of «جنة».

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: The clause «لا تسمع» is a second naʿt (adjective) of {جَنَّةٍ}.

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: (فيها عين جارية) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is a third naʿt (adjective) of {جَنَّةٍ}.

harrat-mujtaba:13-13.t: (فيها سرر مرفوعة) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is a fourth naʿt (adjective) of {جَنَّةٍ}.

harrat-mujtaba:17-17.t: The hamza is interrogative, and the fāʾ is resumptive; the clause «كيف خلقت» is a badal (substitute) of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) from the camels, i.e.: do they not look at the manner of their creation?; «وكيف»: an interrogative noun, a ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (manṣūb) by what follows it; and the verb of looking is suspended (muʿallaq).

harrat-mujtaba:18-18.t: The clause «كيف رُفعت» is a badal (substitute) of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) from «السماء».

harrat-mujtaba:19-19.t: The clause «كيف نُصبت» is a badal (substitute) of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) «من الجبال».

harrat-mujtaba:21-21.t: The clause «فذكِّر» is resumptive, and likewise the clause «إنما أنت مذكِّر».

harrat-mujtaba:22-22.t: (لست عليهم بمسيطر) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is a naʿt (adjective) of {مُذَكِّرٌ}, and the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) in the khabar (predicate) of «ليس»; the preposition «عليهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «مسيطر».

harrat-mujtaba:23-23.t: «من»: a relative noun, excepted from the pronoun of {عَلَيْهِمْ}.

harrat-mujtaba:24-24.t: The clause «فيعذبه» is conjoined to the clause «كفر»; «والعذاب» is nāʾib mafʿūl muṭlaq (substitute for the absolute object).

harrat-mujtaba:25-25.t: (إن إلينا إيابهم) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:26-26.t: (ثم إن علينا حسابهم) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is conjoined to the resumptive one.

mekki-muskil:2-2.t: His saying, the Exalted: (خاشعة): the khabar (predicate) of (وجوه), and that is in the Hereafter.

mekki-muskil:3-3.t: His saying (عاملة): nominative with an implied (هي), and that is in this world; on this interpretation you pause at (خاشعة). (عاملة) may also be a khabar (predicate) after a khabar of (وجوه), so the toil is in the Fire: since they did not toil in this world, Allah made them toil in the Fire; this is the view of al-Ḥasan and Qatāda, and on this view you do not pause at (خاشعة).

mekki-muskil:8-8.t: His saying (وجوه يومئذ ناعمة): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), and (راضية) is a second khabar, or with an implied (هي).

mekki-muskil:23-23.t: His saying (إلا من تولى): (من) is in the position of the nominative [Translator's note: so in the source; an accusative might be expected for a disjoined exception] as a disjoined exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ). It is also said that it is an exception from the same kind, with something implied after (فذكر), i.e. "so remind My servants, except whoever turns away"; or with something implied after (مذكر), i.e. "you are only a reminder to people, except whoever turns away". It is also said that (من) is in the position of the genitive as a badal (substitute) from the hāʾ and mīm in (عليهم).

mekki-muskil:25-25.t: His saying (إن إلينا إيابهم): Abū Jaʿfar read it with the yāʾ doubled, and this is far-fetched, because it is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of (آب يؤوب إيابا), and the origin of the yāʾ [printed «الباء»] is a wāw, but it turned into yāʾ because of the kasra before it. Whoever doubles it would have to say (إوابهم), since it is from wāw, or say (إيوابهم), replacing the first of the doubled letters with a yāʾ, as they said (ديوان) whose origin is (دوان).

muyesser-irab:1-1.t:
﴿هل﴾: an interrogative particle indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn.
﴿أتاك﴾: a past verb indeclinable on the sukūn [Translator's note: so in the source; elsewhere the book parses atā as indeclinable on an implied fatḥa on the alif], and the kāf is a pronoun indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿حديث﴾: fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma.
﴿الغاشية﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr), the sign of its genitive being the kasra.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿وجوه﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma.
﴿يومئذ﴾: yawm: an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿خاشعة﴾, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa; idh: a noun indeclinable (mabnī) on an implied (muqaddar) sukūn, because the place is occupied by the tanwīn of compensation, in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the tanwīn compensates for an omitted clause, the implied form being "yawma idh taghshā al-ghāshiya" (the day when the Overwhelming overwhelms).
﴿خاشعة﴾: khabar (predicate), nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma; or a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿وجوه﴾, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿عاملة﴾: khabar (predicate) of ﴿وجوه﴾, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma; or an adjective (ṣifa) of the mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative, the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma.
﴿ناصبة﴾: khabar of ﴿وجوه﴾, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma; or an adjective of the mubtadaʾ, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma.

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿تصلى﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the implied (muqaddar) ḍamma, and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "hiya". The clause ﴿تصلى﴾ is in the position of the nominative as a fourth khabar (predicate) of ﴿وجوه﴾.
﴿نارًا﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa.
﴿حامية﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿النار﴾, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿تسقى﴾: a passive imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the implied (muqaddar) ḍamma, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "hiya".
﴿من﴾: a preposition indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn.
﴿عين﴾: a genitive noun, the sign of its genitive being the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تسقى﴾.
﴿آنية﴾: an adjective (ṣifa) of ﴿عين﴾, genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the kasra.

muyesser-irab:6-6.t:
﴿ليس﴾: a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa.
﴿لهم﴾: the lām is a preposition indeclinable on the fatḥa, and the pronoun is indeclinable on the ḍamma in the position of the genitive as a genitive noun; the mīm is a particle of the plural indeclinable on the sukūn; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted, fronted khabar (predicate) of laysa.
﴿طعام﴾: the postponed noun (ism) of laysa, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma.
﴿إلا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr), a particle indeclinable on the sukūn.
﴿من﴾: a preposition indeclinable on the sukūn.
﴿ضريع﴾: a genitive noun, the sign of its genitive being the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted adjective (ṣifa) of ﴿طعام﴾, or a badal (substitute) from it, or in the position of the accusative by exception. The clause laysa lahum ṭaʿām is in the position of the nominative as khabar of ﴿وجوه﴾.

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿لا﴾: negative, a particle indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn.
﴿يسمن﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma, and its fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being ﴿هو﴾.
﴿ولا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction indeclinable on the fatḥa, and lā is connective (ṣila) for emphasising the negation, a particle indeclinable on the sukūn.
﴿يغني﴾: an imperfect verb conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿يسمن﴾, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma, and its fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being ﴿هو﴾. The two clauses ﴿لا يسمن ولا يغني﴾ are adjectives (ṣifa) of ﴿ضريع﴾.
﴿من﴾: a preposition indeclinable on the sukūn.
﴿جوع﴾: a genitive noun, the sign of its genitive being the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يغني﴾; or ﴿من﴾ is a connective (ṣila) preposition, and ﴿جوع﴾ is in the place of the accusative as the object of ﴿يغني﴾.

muyesser-irab:8-8.t:
﴿وجوه﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma.
﴿يومئذ﴾: yawm: an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ناعمة﴾, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa; idh: a noun indeclinable (mabnī) on an implied (muqaddar) sukūn, because the place is occupied by the tanwīn of compensation, in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the tanwīn compensates for an omitted clause, the implied form being "yawma idh taghshā al-ghāshiya" (the day when the Overwhelming overwhelms).
﴿ناعمة﴾: khabar (predicate) of ﴿وجوه﴾, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma.

muyesser-irab:9-9.t:
﴿لسعيها﴾: the lām is a preposition indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and saʿy is a genitive noun, the sign of its genitive being the kasra; the pronoun is indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿راضية﴾.
﴿راضية﴾: a second khabar (predicate) of ﴿وجوه﴾, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma.

muyesser-irab:10-10.t:
﴿في﴾: a preposition indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn.
﴿جنة﴾: a genitive noun, the sign of its genitive being the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted second khabar (predicate) of ﴿وجوه﴾.
﴿عالية﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿جنة﴾, genitive (majrūr), the sign of its genitive being the kasra.

muyesser-irab:11-11.t:
﴿لا﴾: negative, a particle indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn.
﴿تسمع﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being ﴿أنت﴾.
﴿فيها﴾: fī is a preposition indeclinable on the sukūn, and the pronoun is indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of the genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تسمع﴾.
﴿لاغية﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa. The clause lā tasmaʿ is in the position of the genitive as a second naʿt (adjective) of ﴿جنة﴾.

muyesser-irab:12-12.t:
﴿فيها﴾: fī is a preposition indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, and the pronoun is indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of the genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate).
﴿عين﴾: postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma.
﴿جارية﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿عين﴾, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma. The clause is a third naʿt of ﴿جنة﴾.

muyesser-irab:13-13.t:
﴿فيها﴾: fī is a preposition indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, and the pronoun is indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of the genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate).
﴿سرر﴾: postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma.
﴿مرفوعة﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿سرر﴾, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma. The clause is a fourth adjective (ṣifa) of ﴿جنة﴾.

muyesser-irab:14-14.t:
﴿وأكواب﴾: the wāw is a conjunction indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and akwāb is a noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿سرر﴾, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma.
﴿موضوعة﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿أكواب﴾, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma.

muyesser-irab:15-15.t:
﴿ونمارق﴾: the wāw is a conjunction indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and akwāb [Translator's note: so in the source, carried over from the previous ayah; the word parsed here is namāriq] is a noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿سرر﴾, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma.
﴿مصفوفة﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿نمارق﴾, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma.

muyesser-irab:16-16.t:
﴿وزرابي﴾: the wāw is a conjunction indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and akwāb [Translator's note: so in the source, carried over from 88:14; the word parsed here is zarābiyy] is a noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿سرر﴾, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma.
﴿مبثوثة﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿زرابي﴾, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma.

muyesser-irab:17-17.t:
﴿أفلا﴾: a resumptive statement with no grammatical position; the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval (istifhām inkārī), a particle indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa; the fāʾ is for conjunction, a particle indeclinable on the fatḥa, conjoining to something implied that the context calls for, the implied form being "a-yunkirūna al-baʿtha fa-lā yanẓurūn" (do they deny the resurrection, and do they not look); and ﴿لا﴾ is negative, a particle indeclinable on the sukūn.
﴿ينظرون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma [Translator's note: so in the source; as one of the five verbs it is nominative by the retention of the nūn], and the wāw is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil (agent).
﴿إلى﴾: a preposition indeclinable on the sukūn.
﴿الإبل﴾: a genitive noun, the sign of its genitive being the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ينظرون﴾.
﴿كيف﴾: an interrogative noun indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿خلقت﴾: a passive past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa; the tāʾ is the tāʾ of the feminine, a particle indeclinable on the sukūn; and the fāʿil [Translator's note: so in the source; with a passive verb, the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is meant] is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "hiya". The clause is a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) from al-ibil.

muyesser-irab:18-18.t:
﴿وإلى﴾: the wāw is a conjunction indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and ilā is a preposition indeclinable on the sukūn.
﴿السماء﴾: a genitive noun, the sign of its genitive being the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ينظرون﴾.
﴿كيف﴾: an interrogative noun indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿رفعت﴾: a passive past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa; the tāʾ is the tāʾ of the feminine, a particle indeclinable on the sukūn; and the fāʿil (agent) [Translator's note: so in the source; the nāʾib fāʿil is meant] is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "hiya". The clause is a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) from ﴿السماء﴾.

muyesser-irab:19-19.t:
﴿وإلى﴾: the wāw is a conjunction indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and ilā is a preposition indeclinable on the sukūn.
﴿الجبال﴾: a genitive noun, the sign of its genitive being the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ينظرون﴾.
﴿كيف﴾: an interrogative noun indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿نصبت﴾: a passive past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa; the tāʾ is the tāʾ of the feminine, a particle indeclinable on the sukūn; and the fāʿil (agent) [Translator's note: so in the source; the nāʾib fāʿil is meant] is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "hiya". The clause is a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) from ﴿الجبال﴾.

muyesser-irab:20-20.t:
﴿وإلى﴾: the wāw is a conjunction indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and ilā is a preposition indeclinable on the sukūn.
﴿الأرض﴾: a genitive noun, the sign of its genitive being the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ينظرون﴾.
﴿كيف﴾: an interrogative noun indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿سطحت﴾: a passive past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa; the tāʾ is the tāʾ of the feminine, a particle indeclinable on the sukūn; and the fāʿil (agent) [Translator's note: so in the source; the nāʾib fāʿil is meant] is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "hiya". The clause is a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) from ﴿الأرض﴾.

muyesser-irab:21-21.t:
﴿فذكر﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (signalling an implied condition), a particle indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and dhakkir is an imperative verb indeclinable on the sukūn; its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "anta", and its object is omitted, i.e. "fa-dhakkirhum" (so remind them).
﴿إنما﴾: inna is an abrogating (nāsikh) particle indeclinable on the fatḥa, restrained (makfūfa) from governing because ﴿ما﴾ has entered upon it; ﴿ما﴾ is a connective (ṣila) particle indeclinable on the sukūn, restraining (kāffa).
﴿أنت﴾: a pronoun indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿مذكر﴾: khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma. The clause ﴿إنما أنت﴾ gives the reason (taʿlīliyya) for the command to remind.

muyesser-irab:22-22.t:
﴿لست﴾: laysa is an inert (jāmid), abrogating (nāsikh) past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and the tāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the nominative as its noun (ism).
﴿عليهم﴾: ʿalā is a preposition indeclinable on the sukūn, and the pronoun is a pronoun indeclinable on the kasra in the position of the genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿مسيطر﴾.
﴿بمسيطر﴾: the bāʾ is a connective (ṣila) preposition indeclinable on the kasra, and musayṭir is a noun genitive by the bāʾ in form and accusative (manṣūb) by position, because it is the khabar (predicate) of ﴿ليس﴾. The clause ﴿لست عليهم بمسيطر﴾ is resumptive by way of explanation (istiʾnāf bayānī), with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:23-23.t:
﴿إلا﴾: a particle of exception, a particle indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn.
﴿من﴾: a relative noun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the accusative as excepted from the object of ﴿فذكر﴾, or from the hāʾ in ﴿عليهم﴾; or the exception is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), ﴿إلا﴾ meaning lākin with its governing cancelled, and ﴿من﴾ is a relative noun indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), its khabar (predicate) being the clause ﴿فيعذبه﴾.
﴿تولى﴾: a past verb indeclinable on an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa, and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa". The clause ﴿تولى﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.
﴿وكفر﴾: the wāw is a conjunction indeclinable on the fatḥa, and kafara is a past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa; the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "huwa". The clause ﴿كفر﴾ is conjoined to ﴿تولى﴾, with no grammatical position. On the view that the exception is disconnected, the clause ﴿إلا من تولى وكفر﴾ is in the position of the accusative.

muyesser-irab:24-24.t:
﴿فيعذبه﴾: the fāʾ is linking (rābiṭa), because of the sense of condition contained in the relative noun, a particle indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa; yuʿadhdhibuhu is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma, and the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object). On the view that the exception is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), the clause ﴿فيعذبه﴾ is in the position of the nominative as khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) man.
﴿الله﴾: the Name of Majesty, fāʿil (agent), nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma.
﴿العذاب﴾: standing in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa; it is a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar).
﴿الأكبر﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿العذاب﴾, accusative, the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa.

muyesser-irab:25-25.t:
﴿إن﴾: an abrogating (nāsikh) particle indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa.
﴿إلينا﴾: ilā is a preposition indeclinable on the sukūn, and the pronoun is indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of the genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are in the position of the nominative as the fronted khabar (predicate) of ﴿إن﴾.
﴿إيابهم﴾: the postponed noun (ism) of inna, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa; the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and the mīm is a particle of the plural, indeclinable on the sukūn. The clause has no grammatical position because it gives the reason (taʿlīl) for ﴿العذاب الأكبر﴾.

muyesser-irab:26-26.t:
﴿ثم﴾: a conjunction for delay, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa.
﴿إن﴾: an abrogating (nāsikh) particle indeclinable on the fatḥa.
﴿علينا﴾: ʿalā is a preposition indeclinable on the sukūn, and the pronoun is indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of the genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are in the position of the nominative as the fronted khabar (predicate) of ﴿إن﴾.
﴿حسابهم﴾: the postponed noun (ism) of inna, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa; the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and the mīm is a particle of the plural, indeclinable on the sukūn. The clause is conjoined to what precedes it, with no grammatical position.

nahhas-irab:1-1.t: The exegetes hold that the meaning of حديث and خبر is the same; and this indicates that the meaning of حدثنا and أخبرنا is the same. This is also indicated by يَوْمَئِذٍ تُحَدِّثُ أَخْبارَها [al-Zalzala: 4], because the meaning of تحدّث and تخبّر is the same. The interpreters have two views about الغاشية. Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: الغاشية is one of the names of the Day of Resurrection. Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: الغاشية is the Fire. Abū Jaʿfar said: The two views are close, because the Resurrection overwhelms people with its terrors, and the Fire at the Resurrection overwhelms people with what is in it.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t:
Abū Jaʿfar said: There are four readings of it, one of them irregular (shādhdh), and four views [on its meaning], one of them irregular. Ibn Kathīr and Nāfiʿ read لا تُسْمَعُ فِيها لاغِيَةٌ with tāʾ and لاغية in the nominative. Ibn Muḥayṣin read «لا يُسمع فيها لاغيةٌ» with yāʾ and the nominative. Abū Jaʿfar, ʿĀṣim, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read لا تَسْمَعُ فِيها لاغِيَةً with fatḥa on the tāʾ. The irregular reading is لا تَسْمَعُ فِيها لاغِيَةً in the sense of "the faces will not hear in it", what is meant being their owners; the faces have been mentioned before. [Translator's note: the source prints all the Quranic forms in this entry in the standard vocalisation «لا تَسْمَعُ فِيها لاغِيَةً», so the vowelling of the variants has been supplied from the descriptions. The account of the readings is also confused in the source: the "irregular" reading is described in the same terms as the third, and the readers named do not fully match the usual transmission.] The first reading gathers the meanings most fully. The second reading is with the masculine, because لاغية and لغو are one. The third reading is "the faces will not hear". As for the four views: from Ibn ʿAbbās, لاغية is harm and falsehood; Mujāhid said: لاغية is abuse; Qatāda said: لاغية is falsehood and sinful talk. Abū Jaʿfar said: These three views are close in meaning, i.e. all of it is idle, false talk. It was also said: لاغية is figurative (majāz) [i.e. "a person of idle talk"]. Al-Akhfash Saʿīd said: as al-Ḥuṭayʾa said: [majzūʾ al-kāmil] 560-
وغررتني وزعمت أنّ ... ك لابن بالصّيف تامر
(You deceived me and claimed that you were one with milk in summer and one with dates.)
Al-Farrāʾ said: لاغية means one who swears falsely. Abū Jaʿfar said: This view is irregular, because it departs from the view of the exegetes, and no one is free to depart from their body in what they have said, even if his view is possible.

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: العين is feminine; its masculine has been reported, as the poet said: [al-basīṭ] 561- والعين بالإثمد الحاريّ مكحول (And the eye is lined with kohl of al-Ḥīra.) Al-Aṣmaʿī knew nothing for العين but the feminine. Abū Jaʿfar said: That is correct. There are two views on this verse. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: what has no sign of the feminine and is not really feminine, you may treat as masculine, as in هذا نار and ذاك دار. Al-Aṣmaʿī said: مكحول refers to the eyebrow, because it has been mentioned before.

nahhas-irab:13-13.t: That is, so that one may look from on top of his couch towards what Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, has bestowed on him of His blessings. [Translator's note: the source reads «لينظروا إلى الله», which seems to be a corruption; rendered here according to the evident sense.]

nahhas-irab:14-14.t: It was said: [the cups are placed] at the sides of the spring, filled.

nahhas-irab:15-15.t: That is, [the cushions are lined up] one beside another.

nahhas-irab:16-17.t:
وَزَرابِيُّ مَبْثُوثَةٌ (16): the singular is زربيّة. [Translator's note: the source has «زريبة», presumably a misprint.] Al-Farrāʾ ] [Translator's note: a stray bracket appears here in the source.] said: they are carpets with pile. He said: مبثوثة means many. أَفَلا يَنْظُرُونَ إِلَى الْإِبِلِ كَيْفَ خُلِقَتْ (17): there are two views on its meaning. One of them is that it is the clouds; the correct view is that it is the camels, and that is what is known in the speech of the Arabs. Qatāda said: When Allah described the bliss of Paradise, the people of misguidance wondered at that, so Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, revealed: أَفَلا يَنْظُرُونَ إِلَى الْإِبِلِ كَيْفَ خُلِقَتْ (17); camels were part of the livelihood of the Arabs and what they hoped for. Abū Jaʿfar said:
The meaning is: Will they not reflect, and so know that He who created these things is able to create whatever He wills?

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: That is, how it was raised above them without pillars that they can see, so that they may infer from it the greatness of His power.

nahhas-irab:19-19.t: That is, they were set up erect, not falling.

nahhas-irab:2-3.t:
وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ خاشِعَةٌ (2): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). Qatāda said: humbled in the Fire, meaning abased.
The interpreters differed about His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: عامِلَةٌ ناصِبَةٌ (3). Some of them said: labouring and toiling in this world; this is [so] interpreted because it is the view of ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him. Its implied form in Arabic is: "faces on that day will be humbled" — and the statement is complete — then He said عاملة, i.e. they are in this world «labouring, toiling». It is also possible that the implied form is "labouring, toiling faces will on that day be humbled", i.e. on the Day of Resurrection, خاشِعَةٌ being the khabar of the mubtadaʾ; it is permissible to begin with an indefinite noun because the meaning concerns the disbelievers, even though the statement is made about the faces. ʿIkrima said:
Labouring in this world in acts of disobedience to Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, toiling in the Fire. On this [view] the implied form is that the complete stop (tamām) is عاملة. The view of al-Ḥasan and Qatāda is that these faces at the Resurrection will be humbled, labouring, toiling, and that since they did not labour in this world, Allah will make them labour in the Fire and make them toil. On this [view], عاملة ناصبة are naʿt (adjective) of خاشعة, or a khabar. This is a good answer, because it does not require any implication, fronting or postponing.

nahhas-irab:20-21.t:
Qatāda said: [سُطِحَتْ means] it was spread out.
فَذَكِّرْ: the object is omitted because the hearer knows it, i.e. remind My servants of My proofs and My signs. إِنَّما أَنْتَ مُذَكِّرٌ, i.e. nothing is incumbent on you but reminding.

nahhas-irab:22-22.t:
Ibn Zayd said: That is, you are not [the one to] bring them back to faith. From Ibn ʿAbbās: بمسيطر means "a tyrant"...
Abū Jaʿfar said: Its origin is with sīn, derived from السطر ("line"), because the meaning of السطر is that which does not go beyond the thing, being prevented from that. One says تسيطر when he gained dominance; ṣād is substituted for the sīn because ṭāʾ comes after it. It was said: it is abrogated by His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: فَاقْتُلُوا الْمُشْرِكِينَ حَيْثُ وَجَدْتُمُوهُمْ [al-Tawba: 5]. It was also said: it is not abrogated, because when they profess Islam they are left as they are and he is not given dominance over them, as was read [in transmission] to Aḥmad ibn Shuʿayb, from ʿAmr ibn Manṣūr, from Abū Nuʿaym, from Sufyān, from Abū al-Zubayr, from Jābir, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: «I have been commanded to fight people until they say: there is no god but Allah. When they say: there is no god but Allah, they have protected their blood and their wealth from me, except by its right, and their reckoning is with Allah.» Then he recited إِنَّما أَنْتَ مُذَكِّرٌ لَسْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ بِمُصَيْطِرٍ (22) بمسيطر». [Translator's note: the closing «بمسيطر»» is a stray repetition in the source.]

nahhas-irab:23-23.t: إِلَّا مَنْ تَوَلَّى is in the position of the accusative as an exception not of the [kind of the] first (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), i.e. but whoever turns away and turns aside from the remembrance of Allah وَكَفَرَ, Allah will punish him. It may also be in the position of the accusative as an exception from the omitted object, i.e. "so remind My servants, except whoever turns away and disbelieves", as you say: "admonish people, except whoever turns away from you and does not accept from you". It may also be an exception in the sense of "you are a reminder to people, except whoever turns away". A fourth view is that مَن is in the position of the genitive as a badal (substitute) for the hāʾ and mīm in عليهم.

nahhas-irab:24-24.t: [الْعَذابَ الْأَكْبَرَ] is the punishment of Hell.

nahhas-irab:25-25.t: Abū Jaʿfar read إِنَّ إِلَيْنا إِيَّابَهُمْ with doubling (tashdīd). [Translator's note: the source prints the word without the doubling sign, as in the standard reading.] It was said: it is a solecism, because it is from آب يئوب, so if it were doubled it would be إوّابهم, and it would become إيوابهم, as one says ديوان, whose original is دوّان; the evidence for that is their saying دواوين in the plural.

nahhas-irab:26-26.t: That is, their reckoning for their disbelief, so that He may requite them for that.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: تَصْلى ناراً حامِيَةً (4) is the reading of the majority, except Abū ʿAmr, who read تُصْلى; we know of no one else who read it. He argued from تُسقى. [Translator's note: the source prints Abū ʿAmr's reading as «تَصْلى», identical to the majority reading; the passive form is supplied according to the argument.] The two meanings are one, because she is made to burn (تُصلى) and so she burns (تَصلى).

nahhas-irab:5-5.t:
ʿAṭāʾ said: [آنِيَةٍ means] its heat has reached its utmost. Ibn Zayd said: آنية means present. Abū Jaʿfar said:
The known view is the first. آنية here differs in its underlying form from His saying يُطافُ عَلَيْهِمْ بِآنِيَةٍ [al-Insān: 15], even though the pronunciation is the same, because in بآنية (vessels) the second alif is a substitute for the hamza, whereas in the other آنية the alif is added; its pattern is فاعلة, while the pattern of the former is أفعلة.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t:
The interpreters differed about the explanation of الضريع. Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said:
الضريع is a tree of fire. Ibn Zayd said: الضريع is thorns of fire; among the Arabs it is dry thorns without leaves. From ʿIkrima: الضريع is stones. From al-Ḥasan two views: one is that الضريع is al-zaqqūm; the other is that الضريع is what makes whoever eats it humble (يضرع) and abased, because of its bitterness and coarseness. Abū Jaʿfar said: This view combines all the views. ʿAṭāʾ said: الضريع is al-shibriq. Abū Jaʿfar said: This is the view the lexicographers reported. الشبرق is a very thorny plant that camels shun.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: That is, it does not satisfy hunger.

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: [وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ ناعِمَةٌ is] a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). It comes without a wāw; had it been with a wāw, it would have been conjoining a clause to a clause.

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: Abū Jaʿfar said: The implied form would be "with the reward of its striving, well pleased". The accusative is permissible for راضية.

safi-cedvel:1-1.t:
* I'rab:
(هل) is a particle of interrogation to arouse eagerness «[Note: or it means قد, to convey information]»; the clause has no grammatical position (inceptive).

safi-cedvel:2-7.t:
* I'rab:
(وجوه) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative, whose khabar (predicate) is the clause تصلى «[Note: Beginning with an indefinite noun is permissible because it has been qualified.]». (يومئذ) is an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān) annexed to a noun of time, accusative — or indeclinable (mabnī) — attached to (خاشعة). (خاشعة، عاملة، ناصبة) are nuʿūt (adjectives) of وجوه, nominative. (من عين) is attached to (تسقى).
Clause: «وجوه ... تصلى» has no grammatical position (explanatory resumptive).
And the clause: «تصلى ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (وجوه).
And the clause: «تسقى ... » is in the position of nominative as a second khabar of (وجوه).
Verses 6–7: (لهم) is attached to the khabar of ليس. (إلّا) is for restriction «[Note: or for exception, and (من ضريع) is an adjective of the implied excepted noun or of the implied badal, i.e. "except food — or food, in the nominative — from ضريع".]». (من ضريع) is attached to an adjective of (طعام). (لا) is negative in both places. (جوع) is genitive in form, accusative in position, as a direct object (mafʿūl bihi), because the verb is made to include the meaning "it repels".
Clause: «ليس لهم طعام ... » is in the position of nominative as a third khabar ..., and the pronoun in (لهم) refers to the owners of the faces.
And the clause: «لا يسمن ... » is in the position of genitive as an naʿt (adjective) of ضريع.
And the clause: «لا يغني ... » is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause لا يسمن.

* Morphology:
(3) ناصبة: plural of ناصب, an active participle from the triliteral نصب meaning "to be weary"; its wazn is فاعل.
(4) حامية: feminine of الحامي, an active participle from the triliteral حمي; its wazn is فاعل.
(6) ضريع: the name of a kind of thorn, said to be the shibraq while it is green; when it dries it is ضريع, which no beast eats.

* Rhetoric:
Kināya (metonymy): in His words, the Exalted, «لَيْسَ لَهُمْ طَعامٌ إِلَّا مِنْ ضَرِيعٍ».
The statement contains majāz or kināya, meaning food that camels and other animals which enjoy grazing on thorns find disagreeable; this is not inconsistent with its also being زقوم or غسلين. It has also been said that the meaning is that they have no food at all, since ضريع is not food even for beasts, let alone people, as one says: "So-and-so has no shade but the sun," meaning he has no shade. On this is taken His saying, the Exalted, «وَلا طَعامٌ إِلَّا مِنْ غِسْلِينٍ».
The art of tatmīm (completion): in His words, the Exalted, «لا يُسْمِنُ وَلا يُغْنِي مِنْ جُوعٍ».
His words «وَلا يُغْنِي مِنْ جُوعٍ» are a clause that cannot be dropped from the discourse, because when He said «لا يُسْمِنُ», someone might imagine that this food, which is not of the kind of human food, lacks the quality of fattening but retains the quality of satisfying; so the clause «وَلا يُغْنِي مِنْ جُوعٍ» came to complete the intended meaning, namely that this food lacks the quality of giving fatness and strength, just as it lacks the quality of removing and dispelling hunger.

safi-cedvel:8-16.t:
* I'rab:
(وجوه يومئذ ناعمة) is like وجوه يومئذ خاشعة «[Note: in verse (2) of this sūra]». (لسعيها) is attached to (راضية), the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (وجوه). (في جنة) is attached to an omitted second khabar of وجوه «[Note: or it is the khabar and (راضية) a second naʿt]». (لا) is a negative particle. (فيها) is attached to (تسمع) «[Note: or attached to a ḥāl from لاغية, i.e. "a group speaking idly in it"]». The second (فيها) is attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (عين), and the third (فيها) is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (سرر), which is conjoined to it. (أكواب، نمارق، زرابيّ) are nominative like it.
Clause: «وجوه ... راضية» has no grammatical position (another explanatory resumptive).
And the clause: «لا تسمع ... » is in the position of genitive as a second naʿt (adjective) of جنة.
And the clause: «فيها عين جارية ... » is in the position of genitive as a third naʿt of جنة.
And the clause: «فيها سرر ... » is in the position of genitive as a fourth naʿt.

* Morphology:
(8) ناعمة: feminine of ناعم, an active participle from the triliteral نعم; its wazn is فاعل.
(11) لاغية: feminine of لاغ, an active participle of (لغا يلغو). In لاغية there is a weakening by substitution: the original is لاغوة, the wāw was changed to yāʾ because it is vowelled after a kasra. Its wazn is فاعلة, and the wazn of لاغ is فاع. It has also been said that (لاغية) is a maṣdar like العافية.
(14) موضوعة: feminine of موضوع, a passive participle from the triliteral وضع; its wazn is مفعول.
(15) نمارق: plural of نمرقة, a noun meaning a cushion; its wazn is فعللة (with ḍamma on the fā' and the first lām), which in one dialect may both be kasra; the wazn of نمارق is فعالل (with fatḥa on the fāʾ and kasra on the first lām).
(16) زرابيّ: plural of زربيّة, a non-derived noun for a kind of carpets and rugs; it is also said to be the plural of زربيّ (with ḍamma or kasra on the zāy — as in al-Qāmūs — and shadda on the yāʾ), and it is also said that the zāy takes all three vowels in both. Its wazn is فعليل or فعليلة, and the wazn of زرابيّ is فعاليل (with fatḥa on the fāʾ).
(مبثوثة) feminine of مبثوث, a passive participle from the triliteral بثّ; its wazn is مفعول.

safi-cedvel:17-20.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) is for rebuking interrogation. (الفاء) is a conjunction. (لا) is a negative particle. (إلى الإبل) is attached to (ينظرون). (كيف) is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), its operator being the verb that follows it. (إلى السماء) is attached to (ينظرون), and likewise (إلى الجبال، إلى الأرض). (كيف) is like the first in both places.
Clause: «ينظرون ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to an implied resumptive clause), i.e.:
"Do they deny, and so not look ...?"
And the clause: «خلقت ... » is in the position of genitive as a badal ishtimāl (inclusive substitute) from الإبل, i.e. "they look at the creation of the camels" «[Note: and in the marginal note of al-Jamal: "ينظرون is made transitive to الإبل by (إلى), and transitive to (كيف خلقت ...) by way of suspension (taʿlīq). A clause containing an interrogative may be a substitute for the noun before it even if that noun contains no interrogative ... When the operator is suspended from what contains an interrogative, the interrogative does not remain in its true sense ..." End of quotation.]» or "at the manner of their creation".
And the clause: «رفعت ... » is in the position of genitive as a badal ishtimāl from السماء.
And the clause: «نصبت ... » is in the position of genitive as a badal ishtimāl from الجبال.
And the clause: «سطحت ... » is in the position of genitive as a badal ishtimāl from الأرض.

* Benefits:
- A clause occurring as a substitute for a single word:
In this verse (أَفَلا يَنْظُرُونَ إِلَى الْإِبِلِ كَيْفَ خُلِقَتْ) the clause (كَيْفَ خُلِقَتْ) occurs as a badal for الإبل, and on that basis the grammarians laid down a rule: "a clause may occur as a substitute for a single word". Here is what Ibn Hishām cited in al-Mughnī on this point: In His words, the Exalted (أَفَلا يَنْظُرُونَ إِلَى الْإِبِلِ كَيْفَ خُلِقَتْ), it is not valid for (كيف) to be a badal of الإبل, because a preposition entering كيف is anomalous, and moreover it was not heard with إلى but with على; and because إلى is attached to what precedes it, which would require that a verb preceding the interrogative operate on it; and because the clause after it would then be unconnected, whereas it is accusative by what follows it as a ḥāl, the verb of looking being suspended; it and what follows it are a badal ishtimāl of الإبل, the meaning being "at the camels, the manner of their creation". Similar is His saying, the Exalted (أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلى رَبِّكَ كَيْفَ مَدَّ الظِّلَّ), and similar to both, as a substitution of a clause containing كيف for a single noun, is the verse of al-Farazdaq:
إلى الله أشكو بالمدينة حاجة ... وبالشام أخرى كيف يلتقيان
(To Allah I complain of a need in Medina and another in Syria — how can the two meet?)
that is, "I complain of these two needs, the impossibility of their meeting".

safi-cedvel:21-26.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) links the apodosis of an implied condition. (إنّما) is the restrictive particle (kāffa) with what it restricts (makfūfa). (عليهم) is attached to مسيطر. (مسيطر) is genitive in form, accusative in position, as the khabar of ليس. (إلّا) is for exception «[Note: disconnected (munqaṭiʿ) from the pronoun in (عليهم), or connected (muttaṣil) from the implied object of ذكّر, i.e. "remind My servants"]». (من) is a relative noun in the position of accusative as the excepted «[Note: or it means لكن, in which case (من) is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause يعذّبه, with the fāʾ redundant, and the clause is resumptive or in the position of accusative as a disconnected exception, in the view of Ibn Kharūf]». (الفاء) is a conjunction. (العذاب) is an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq), accusative. (إلينا) is attached to the khabar of inna, and likewise (علينا) is the second khabar of inna.
Clause: «ذكّر ... » is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if the disbelievers do not take heed of the signs of Allah's power, then remind them of them".
And the clause: «إنّما أنت مذكّر ... » has no grammatical position (causal).
And the clause: «لست عليهم بمسيطر» has no grammatical position (explanatory resumptive).
And the clause: «تولّى ... » has no grammatical position (ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (من)).
And the clause: «كفر ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the clause تولّى).
And the clause: «يعذّبه الله» has no grammatical position (conjoined to an implied resumptive clause, i.e. "He detains him and punishes him").
And the clause: «إنّ إلينا إيابهم ... » has no grammatical position (giving the reason for the reckoning).
And the clause: «إنّ علينا حسابهم» has no grammatical position (conjoined to the causal clause).

* Morphology:
(21) مذكّر: an active participle from the quadriliteral ذكّر; its wazn is مفعّل (with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the doubled ʿayn).
(25) إيابهم: a samāʿī maṣdar of the triliteral آب يئوب (the pattern of نصر); it has another maṣdar, أوبة, on the wazn فعلة (with fatḥa and sukūn); the wazn of إياب is فعال (with kasra on the fāʾ). It contains a change by substitution: the original is إواب; the letter before the wāw has a kasra, so it was changed into yāʾ ...

* Rhetoric:
The secret of fronting the adverbial: in His words, the Exalted «إِنَّ إِلَيْنا إِيابَهُمْ ثُمَّ إِنَّ عَلَيْنا حِسابَهُمْ».
Its meaning is intensification of the threat: that their return is only to the Compeller, who is able to take vengeance, and that their reckoning is incumbent on none but Him, who reckons even over the smallest speck and the thinnest membrane.

* Benefits:
The excepted clause:
Ibn Hishām says in al-Mughnī: The grammarians have mentioned that the clauses that have a position in i'rab are seven. The truth is that they are nine. What they neglected is the excepted clause and the clause to which predication is attributed.
As for the excepted: such as His words, the Exalted (لَسْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ بِمُصَيْطِرٍ إِلَّا مَنْ تَوَلَّى وَكَفَرَ فَيُعَذِّبُهُ اللَّهُ الْعَذابَ الْأَكْبَرَ). Ibn Kharūf said: (من) is a mubtadaʾ and (فَيُعَذِّبُهُ اللَّهُ) is the khabar, and the clause is in the position of accusative as a disconnected exception. And al-Farrāʾ said, regarding the reading of some (فشربوا منه إلا قليل منهم), that (قليل) is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e. "they did not drink". A group said regarding (إلا امرأتك) in the nominative that it is a mubtadaʾ and the clause after it its khabar. Our saying is not among the excepted clauses:
(ما مررت بأحد إلا زيد خير منه) because the clause here is a ḥāl from أحد by agreement, or an adjective of it according to al-Akhfash, and in (ما علمت زيدا إلا يفعل الخير) it is a direct object.
